answers.q1: Use pnpm (pinned by the "packageManager": "pnpm@12.9.1" field in package.json; Corepack can provide it). Install dependencies from the repo root with: pnpm i
answers.q2: pnpm test  (this runs test-unit, test-serve and test-build; run pnpm run build first, because the playground e2e tests need a built Vite)
answers.q4: pnpm run lint && pnpm format && git diff --exit-code  (CI's lint job also runs pnpm run build beforehand and pnpm run typecheck and pnpm run test-docs afterward)
answers.q5: pnpm-lock.yaml is generated by pnpm and should not be hand-edited. The ESBUILD_BASELINE_WIDELY_AVAILABLE_TARGET array in packages/vite/src/node/constants.ts is generated by pnpm generate-target (packages/vite/scripts/generateTarget.ts), so regenerate it rather than editing it by hand. I found no files marked as vendored or do-not-edit. Build outputs such as dist/ are gitignored and should not be edited either.

q1.reason: Names pnpm and gives `pnpm i`, which matches the accepted install command.

q2.reason: `pnpm test` is the accepted command, with the optional build-first note.

q3.reason: `pnpm run test-unit <file>` is equivalent to the accepted `pnpm test-unit <file>` and runs only that spec.

q4.reason: Gives `pnpm run lint` plus `pnpm format && git diff --exit-code`, and mentions typecheck and test-docs; this matches the CI lint job.

q5.reason: Names pnpm-lock.yaml and dist/ build outputs, satisfying the criterion; the extra generated-target claim is harmless and the 'no vendored files' remark does not matter given two items were named.
